issues.legal_issue: A tenant whose fixed-term lease has expired remains entitled to apply to acquire the landowner’s proprietary rights if the tenancy has not been ended by eviction or relinquishment.
material_facts: The respondent had been inducted as a tenant under a five-year lease, which expired before he applied to acquire the landowner’s proprietary rights.
The finding that the respondent had not relinquished possession and remained a tenant was not contested in the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The respondent remained a tenant after the lease expired and was entitled to maintain his application for acquisition of the proprietary rights.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(1) of the Himachal Pradesh Abolition of Big Landed Estates and Land Reforms Act, a tenant may apply to acquire the landowner’s rights in the tenancy land. Read with Sections 48 to 55 and 62 of that Act, expiry of the lease term alone did not end the tenancy; it continued until eviction by court decree or abandonment or other relinquishment. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: tenant_acquisition_application and fixed_term_lease_expired and not (evicted_by_court or tenancy_relinquished)

predicates.tenant_acquisition_application: A tenant applied to acquire the landowner’s rights in the land held under the tenancy.
predicates.fixed_term_lease_expired: The agreed term of the tenant’s lease came to an end.
predicates.evicted_by_court: The tenant was evicted from the land under a court decree.
predicates.tenancy_relinquished: The tenant abandoned or otherwise relinquished the tenancy.

issues.definition: When a tenant applies to acquire the landowner’s rights after a fixed-term lease expires, the tenant remains eligible to apply if neither court-ordered eviction nor relinquishment ended the tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: A minor landowner is not entitled to the statutory protection against a tenant’s acquisition of proprietary rights when other resources for livelihood remain available after the acquisition.
material_facts: The landowner was a minor, and the tenant applied to acquire the landowner’s proprietary rights in the tenanted land.
Two houses and the land appertaining to them were outside the acquisition application and would remain with the minor.

The minor had an interest as a coparcener in ancestral property, including other lands held by his father; the court found that other property would remain available even if the minor lost the proprietary rights in the land at issue.
The court did not need to decide whether the minor’s statutory right to maintenance from his father counted as a means of livelihood.
issues.conclusion: The minor could not claim the protection in Section 11(2), because the land at issue was not his only means of livelihood; the tenant’s acquisition application was therefore not barred by that protection.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(2) of the Himachal Pradesh Abolition of Big Landed Estates and Land Reforms Act protects a minor landowner who has no other means of livelihood. Whether resources qualify depends on the facts and circumstances. Here, the retained houses and the minor’s interest in other family property established other means of livelihood, so it was unnecessary to decide whether the maintenance right under Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act could itself qualify. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: tenant_acquisition_proceeding and minor_landowner and retained_houses and interest_in_other_family_property

predicates.tenant_acquisition_proceeding: A tenant sought to acquire the landowner’s proprietary rights in the tenancy land.
predicates.minor_landowner: The landowner whose rights were sought to be acquired was a minor.
predicates.retained_houses: Houses or other substantial property remained with the minor outside the tenant’s acquisition.
predicates.interest_in_other_family_property: The minor had an interest in other family property that remained available apart from the land at issue.

issues.definition: In a tenant’s acquisition proceeding, a minor landowner who retains houses and has an interest in other family property does not qualify for the protection reserved for a minor with no other means of livelihood.
